minutes.headline: Building committee approved the architects' first-phase TCP design work, with a June decision on November Town Meeting.
minutes.summary: The TCP Building Design Committee met remotely to review the architects' proposal for pre-design tasks that can be done without entering the closed building, such as site survey, drone and lidar work, code review and civil analysis. Members debated whether to start now or wait about 30 days given COVID-19 budget uncertainty. A motion to approve the proposal and revisit the November Town Meeting timeline in early June was moved and put to a roll call; the next meeting was set for June 1.

what_happened.line: The TCP Building Design Committee approved the architects' proposal to start design work on the external aspects of the TCP project, by roll call.
The approval also asks the architects to look into building access sooner and to reevaluate the November Town Meeting target in the first week of June.
The architects said every task sits within the original contract and appropriation and was split out so the committee could choose how much to commit.
Members raised concern about spending before the economic outlook is known; a possible state aid cut was raised, and the project's funding source and FY21 capacity were discussed.
The next committee meeting was set for June 1 at 6 p.m., and the architects are to check in with the chair in about two weeks.

why_it_matters: Whether the TCP project goes to voters at the November Town Meeting depends on a June decision, and the work approved here feeds the cost estimate that Town Meeting would be asked to act on.

The project money sits in an authorized account funded earlier from free cash, so it returns to the budget only if Town Meeting rescinds that authorization; any shortfall would fall on the town budget, mostly taxes.
